name: Priorities first
does: Each partner ranks wedding parts on their own. The top 3 become protected lines. Every new expense gets checked against them.

name: Real budget
does: Starts from your own money (bank balance, savings, family pledges), not national averages. El Paso prices. Full 79-line list including the forgotten items. A 10% cushion line from day one. Honeymoon line protected. Venue goes first because it sets the date, headcount and rentals. Travel gets its own line.

name: Guests are money
does: Live cost per guest. Move the guest slider and watch the total change. Warns that you pay for the guaranteed headcount, not who shows up.

name: Quote decoder
does: Paste or photograph a vendor quote. AI adds the service charge, tax on that charge, tips, overtime, vendor meals, corkage and travel, then shows the true cost, what it does to your budget and cost per guest, vague words to pin down, and questions to ask before signing.

name: Payment calendar with bank sync
does: Every deposit and final payment on one calendar, pulled from the quotes. The bank link marks a payment paid when it clears. Warns before money is due, and warns if a vendor's bank details change.

name: Find money
does: Reads the bank feed for subscriptions and repeat charges. "Cancel these and you have $X a month for the wedding." Sets a monthly wedding savings amount and shows the months to the goal. Warns before a vendor gets paid with credit you cannot pay off. Cash gifts count as a bonus, never as funding.

name: Family pledges
does: Padrino-style list. Relatives pledge named items (cake, music, dress). Shows pledged vs received. Notes any strings attached (guest list say, planning say) and the split rules between families. In-kind help counts.

name: Over-budget fixer
does: When you go over, it suggests cuts ranked by how rarely people regret them (favors, place cards, flower reuse, cake swaps first) and protects the lines people regret cutting (photos, music, food, hair and makeup). Shows the guest cut that would cover it.

name: Contract exposure
does: Reads the contract's cancellation terms. "If you cancel on June 1 you owe $2,400." Flags date-change and force majeure terms, and asks what happens if the vendor cancels.

name: Quote compare
does: All quotes for one category side by side at true cost, plus a red-flag checklist.

name: Book-by dates
does: From the wedding date, when each vendor must be booked.

name: Low-budget starting plans
does: Start from a real wedding: $3,000 backyard, $4,847 backyard for 80, $11,000 park wedding.

name: Couple money talk
does: Short prompts before the first deposit: debt, accounts, spending styles, who does which task.

name: Plan B line
does: A weather and backup line priced into the cushion.
